doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Producers pressing her to change her approach
summary: Early in her career producers pushed commercial changes; now she simply states her position.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Excellent. As a headliner and an artist, I’m going to surmise that you have a certain amount of pressure on you to keep working, you have a family and you have side musicians that you want to provide gigs for. Over the years have you ever had to be in a situation where a producer or people pulling the strings wanted you to change your approach because they thought it would be more financially rewarding?

Um hum. That’s happened. Yeah. That happened early on in my career. And not so much now. Once in a while, I’ve had a producer to try that on. But that was a very short conversation you know without even getting — I didn’t even have to get angry about it or even concerned. I just stated where I was and where I was staying. And it was the end of that. And we went on about recording the way I wanted to hear this particular song. Yeah once in a while I’ll run into that.
